title: Houston Family Recovers After Neighbor Rescues Children from Burning Townhouse
text: Houston Family Recovers After Neighbor Rescues Children from Burning Townhouse A family of four was hospitalized following a fire in a Houston townhouse complex where neighbors helped rescue children and a mother who jumped from a third-story window to escape the flames. Four family members were hospitalized early Thursday morning after a fire at a Houston townhouse complex in the Greater Heights. FOX 26's Jillian Hartmann spoke to a neighbor who says he helped three of the family members when they jumped out a window. A family of four is recovering after a fire broke out at a townhome in Houston’s Greater Heights area early Thursday morning. The Houston Fire Department says a neighbor helped rescue two children who jumped from a third-story window to escape the flames. The Houston Fire Department says a neighbor helped rescue two children who jumped from a third-story window to escape the flames. John Bauer says he heard popping noises and noticed an orange glow coming from the home.When he looked outside, he saw a car on fire and immediately called 911. Bauer says he and another neighbor ran toward the home after realizing people could still be inside. They eventually heard screaming coming from the side of the house, where they found a mother and her two daughters. He says he caught the first girl as she jumped, while he and another neighbor helped catch the second child.They also helped the mother as she jumped from the window. Bauer says he is grateful the girls are okay and hopes the parents make a full recovery. A fire at a Houston townhouse in the Greater Heights area left a father in critical condition at the hospital after he helped get his two children and their mother to safety.The father was able to move the burning vehicle out of the garage, but the flames had already spread into the home. The mother also suffered injuries after jumping from the window. Neighbors say the situation unfolded quickly, with people rushing out of their homes to help the family. Brooke Murski says she woke up to screaming and popping noises before looking outside and seeing the car and home on fire.\"It went from zero to 100, and the flames almost engulfed the house,\" Murski said. \"It’s really a miracle that everyone did get out alive. \"Neighbors in a Houston Heights neighborhood came together to help a family of four escape a townhome fire early Thursday morning. FOX 26's Jillian Hartmann spoke to a neighbor who witnessed the fire and the rescue efforts.FOX 26 learned the two girls are okay, but the parents remain hospitalized. Authorities say the mother has back injuries, while the father suffered serious burns and was last reported to be in critical condition.
